articles.headline: Carragher questions Wirtz future in Liverpool XI after latest struggles
articles.description: Jamie Carragher has called on Andoni Iraola to drop Florian Wirtz for Liverpool's clash with Manchester City after describing the midfielder's display against Bournemouth as one of his worst since arriving at Anfield.
articles.headlineJa: キャラガー、最近の不振を受けヴィルツのリヴァプールでの先発定着に疑問符
articles.descriptionJa: ジェイミー・キャラガーは、ボーンマス戦でのフロリアン・ヴィルツのパフォーマンスをアンフィールド加入以来最悪の部類と評し、マンチェスター・シティ戦に向けてアンドニ・イラオラに同MFを外すよう求めました。
articles.body:
Jamie Carragher has called on Andoni Iraola to drop Florian Wirtz for Liverpool's clash with Manchester City after describing the midfielder's display against Bournemouth as one of his worst since arriving at Anfield.

Wirtz struggled to make an impact in Liverpool's 1-0 win at the Vitality Stadium, prompting Carragher to question whether his underwhelming start is simply a matter of form or a sign of a bigger problem.

"That was one of the poorest I've ever seen him in a Liverpool shirt," Carragher said on the Jamie Carragher Podcast.

"I've been critical of the fact that he hasn't got the numbers. But normally when you watch Wirtz, he's neat and tidy, he keeps possession, there's things that you like. He gets out of a tight situation where you're normally expecting your player to lose the ball.

"But the reason I worry is, I don't think Wirtz is in poor form since he came to Liverpool. I actually think what we're seeing is what he is."

Carragher had already voiced his frustration with Wirtz while on commentary during the game, saying of his first-half display, "It's just nothing. Nothing is happening there at all."

The former Liverpool defender said his concerns over Wirtz predated Saturday's performance and pointed to a previous game against Burnley as an example of the lack of attacking threat he believes the midfielder has shown.

"And I was worried for Wirtz probably 12 months ago. And maybe that was a little bit early to say that, but I didn't say it. It was just in the back of my head.

"I commentated on Liverpool away at Burnley and Liverpool won with a late penalty from Mo Salah. And when I was watching that game it was what I've seen for the last 12 months: I don't see how he's going to hurt you. It's just neat and tidy. And in some way, the price tag for that type of player should be half of what Liverpool have paid."

Wirtz arrived at Liverpool amid significant expectations, but Carragher believes the midfielder has considerable ground to make up if he is to become the player the club expected.

"The worry for Wirtz now is that his performances so far, or what he's given Liverpool, is so low. Where we were expecting him was to take Liverpool to another league title, to take Liverpool to a Champions League.

"The gap he's got to get to almost justify what people were expecting, I almost think is too big. You can't get there. Even if he improves a bit and gets there, it's still not what Liverpool thought they were getting."

Carragher also believes Wirtz's role at No. 10 is forcing Szoboszlai into a position that does not suit him.

"And it's not just Wirtz, it's the knock-on effect. So when he plays at No 10, it means Dominik Szoboszlai has to play central midfield. I don't think Szoboszlai is a central-midfield player, I don't."

articles.headline: Man United's Michael Carrick concerned about Benjamin Sesko's latest injury
articles.description: Michael Carrick has raised concerns about Benjamin Sesko's latest injury by revealing the problem is connected to the same shin issue which kept the striker sidelined for more than two months over the summer.
articles.headlineJa: マンチェスター・ユナイテッドのマイケル・キャリック、ベンヤミン・シェシュコの最新の負傷に懸念
articles.descriptionJa: マイケル・キャリックは、ベンヤミン・シェシュコの最新の負傷について、夏に同ストライカーを2か月以上離脱させたのと同じすねの問題に関連していることを明かし、懸念を示しました。
articles.body:
Michael Carrick has raised concerns about Benjamin Sesko's latest injury by revealing the problem is connected to the same shin issue which kept the striker sidelined for more than two months over the summer.

Sesko missed the final three games of last season with the injury which also prevented the 23-year-old from taking part in any of United's preseason fixtures.

He returned as a substitute on the opening weekend against Hull, one of six appearances in all competitions he's made this season.

But after starting the 3-2 Carabao Cup defeat to Brighton on Wednesday, Sesko was absent from the squad against Fulham on Sunday.

And afterwards Carrick revealed the Slovenian is suffering from recurrence of the same shin problem.

"We're not sure with Ben yet," the United head coach said.

"He felt a bit of pain after the game [against Brighton] so we're assessing him. At the moment, he definitely wasn't ready for [Fulham], so I haven't really got any more news to give you at this point. We'll have to see what that brings."

- Cole Palmer withdraws from England's Nations League squad - sources

- Michael Carrick keen to find Man United positives, but there aren't many right now

Carrick will hope that the extended international break gives some of his injured players time to get back to full fitness.

Summer signing Carlos Baleba was on the bench for the first time at Craven Cottage while Matthijs de Ligt made the trip to London, but wasn't fit enough to be named in the squad.

Winger Amad Diallo is yet to play this season. Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo were both named in the England squad, but ongoing issues may mean they are forced to pull out.

articles.headline: Dodgers get better of Giants' bullpen in 3-1 win to sweep three-game series
articles.description: — Kiké Hernández hit a go-ahead RBI double in the seventh inning, Emmet Sheehan did not give up a run in 5 1/3 innings, and the Los Angeles Dodgers beat the San Francisco Giants 3-1 on Sunday to complete a three-game sweep.
articles.headlineJa: ドジャースが3-1でジャイアンツのブルペン陣を攻略、3連戦をスイープ
articles.descriptionJa: キケ・ヘルナンデスが7回に勝ち越しの適時二塁打を放ち、エメット・シーハンが5回1/3を無失点に抑え、ロサンゼルス・ドジャースが日曜日にサンフランシスコ・ジャイアンツを3-1で破り3連戦スイープを達成しました。
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- — Kiké Hernández hit a go-ahead RBI double in the seventh inning, Emmet Sheehan did not give up a run in 5 1/3 innings, and the Los Angeles Dodgers beat the San Francisco Giants 3-1 on Sunday to complete a three-game sweep.


              Hernández jumped on the first pitch he saw from Sam Hentges (1-7), driving in Max Muncy to put the Dodgers ahead 2-1. Muncy pushed an insurance run across with a single in the eighth.


              Kris Bubic (4-2) pitched 2/3 of an inning for the win, and Tanner Scott handled the ninth inning for his 23rd save.


              Sheehan made the most of a bullpen game to strengthen his credentials for making the Dodgers’ postseason roster as a long reliever. He had nine strikeouts against one hit and one walk after taking over from Jack Dreyer in the second inning.


              Matt Wilkinson allowed three hits and no walks while striking out six in five scoreless innings, but the Giants’ bullpen buckled. The 23-year-old left-hander was acquired as part of the trade that sent catcher Patrick Bailey to Cleveland in May.


              Tommy Edman homered to right in the sixth inning to tie the game at 1, tagging reliever Carson Seymour for the 400-foot shot.


              Jonah Cox drew a leadoff walk to help spot the Giants their 1-0 lead. Cox reached second on a bad pickoff attempt by Dreyer before stealing third, and Victor Bericoto’s single drove him home.


              Up next
              Giants: RHP Blade Tidwell (1-2, 4.56 ERA) starts in the opener of a three-game series against the Minnesota Twins on Monday night, facing RHP Bailey Ober (7-6, 4.32).


              Dodgers: Manager Dave Roberts said there would be another bullpen game Tuesday night to start a three-game series against the San Diego Padres, who have yet to set their rotation.


              ------

articles.headline: Why this 3-week international break is longest ever (and why that's a good thing)
articles.description: Fans have grown used to international games interrupting the club season, but this break will be a week longer than before. It's not as bad as it sounds.
articles.headlineJa: 今回の3週間にわたる代表ウィークが過去最長となる理由（そしてそれが良いことである理由）
articles.descriptionJa: ファンはクラブのシーズンが代表戦で中断することに慣れてきていますが、今回のブレイクはこれまでより1週間長くなります。とはいえ、聞いたほど悪いことではありません。
articles.body:
It feels like the new club season has only just begun, and yet we are already having to reckon with the prospect of 2026-27's first international break.

While fans have grown used to matches between national teams providing an early interruption just a few weeks into the campaign, there will be something different about the upcoming round of men's international fixtures: It will be a week longer.

While that may sound like a terrifying prospect to many a fan hooked on the top club competitions such as the UEFA Champions League, Premier League and LaLiga, the situation is not as bad as it sounds. That's because this break is the first to fall under FIFA's reconfigured international match calendar.

- 2026 Ballon d'Or: Full men's, women's shortlists, host city, more

- USMNT's gifted next generation kick-start road to 2030 World Cup

- Messi's emotional Argentina farewell shows he hasn't forgotten criticism

Previously, in the first half of each season there were three separate two-game international breaks held in September, October and November every year, with another the following March. But to minimize disruption to the domestic club schedule across the men's and women's game, FIFA voted unanimously to approve changes to its calendar in 2023. The 2026-27 season will be the first to see these alterations come into effect.

As such, we will now see an extended, 16-day international break taking place between Sept. 21 and Oct. 6 (between Premier League gameweeks 5 and 6) that will allow national teams to fit four matches into one window. This reduces the number of international breaks in the first half of the season from three to two, and limits the total number of weeks that club seasons are put on hold reduced from six to five.

From now on, there will be only three international breaks a season that fall during the domestic campaign. This season, they are as follows:

1. Sept. 21-Oct. 6 (between Premier League gameweeks 5 and 6)

2. Nov. 9-Nov. 17 (between Premier League gameweeks 10 and 11)

3. March 22-March 30 (between Premier League gameweeks 30 and 31)

As per FIFA's updated calendar, the fourth and fifth international breaks of the season come in June and July, once the club season is over. That allows room in the itinerary for international tournaments to take place during a period when most club leagues around the world are not active. For example, the finals of the Concacaf Gold Cup, CAF Africa Cup of Nations and UEFA Nations League will all be held next summer. The one exception to this is the AFC Asian Cup, which will take place in Saudi Arabia next year between Jan. 7 and Feb. 5.

While the changes to the international calendar will certainly have an impact when it comes to limiting the disruption to the domestic season, they don't go far enough for Arsène Wenger, FIFA's chief of global football development. Sept. 18: Josh Allen puts league on notice with 40-point night

by Adam Rank

We had one of the highest-scoring Week 1s in NFL history last week. There was no way we could possibly top that, yeah? Well, I've got news for you, the Buffalo Bills and Detroit Lions accepted the challenge and put up massive numbers on Thursday night.

Josh Allen led the way with more than 40 points to get your week started. We went into the draft season saying Allen was in his own tier and he's proving it early on. Allen had over 300 total yards and five total touchdowns. Allen is the third player in NFL history with nine total touchdowns and no turnovers in his team's first two games of the season. The other two were Patrick Mahomes in 2018 and Peyton Manning in 2013. Both went on to win MVP. Manning's Broncos also set the NFL record for most points in the season.

The Bills are the first team to record 35 points and more than 400 yards of offense in both of their first two games of the season since the Packers in 2020. The Bills have also scored five touchdowns in five red zone drives.

My guy Tristan H. Cockcroft pointed out during our in-game group chat that Allen broke the record for most fantasy points scored in the first two weeks of the season. Breaking the record of ... Ryan Fitzpatrick, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers version (as noted by Field Yates, who knew the answer to Tristan's trivia question).

Our group chat also had an interesting conversation about James Cook III. Is he a trade-high candidate because it's Josh Allen's offense, including goal-line carries -- or do you try to get more shares of Cook, if possible? Put me in the convo for more shares. I want as much of this Bills offense as possible. Especially if D.J. Moore is going to miss time. (Note: Moore is considered day-to-day)

articles.headline: Chiefs laud Kenneth Walker III's impact through 2-0 start
articles.description: For a second straight week, offseason acquisition Kenneth Walker III demonstrated how he has helped revitalize the Kansas City offense, tallying 178 all-purpose yards in the Chiefs' 33-30 overtime win against the Colts.
articles.headlineJa: チーフス、開幕2連勝を支えるケネス・ウォーカー3世の活躍を絶賛
articles.descriptionJa: オフシーズンに獲得したケネス・ウォーカー3世は、コルツに延長戦の末33-30で勝利した試合で計178オールパーパスヤードを記録。2週連続でカンザスシティのオフェンス活性化に大きく貢献していることを証明した。
articles.body:
KANSAS CITY, Mo. -- Before Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes walked off the field Sunday night inside Arrowhead Stadium, he made sure to hug one of his newest teammates: running back Kenneth Walker III.

"K9!" Mahomes shouted, referencing Walker's nickname. 

After the Chiefs' 33-30 overtime win against the Indianapolis Colts, Mahomes made sure to praise Walker, whose 178 all-purpose yards -- along with Mahomes' 382 passing yards -- demonstrated for a second straight week how the reigning Super Bowl MVP has helped revitalize the Kansas City offense. 

The Chiefs were optimistic when they signed Walker that he would add dynamic playmaking to their offense. But he has surpassed expectations, leading all skill-position players in the NFL with 369 all-purpose yards through Kansas City's 2-0 start.

"It's fun for me," Mahomes said of playing next to Walker. "Him running the ball and our offensive line driving off the ball the way they're driving off, it's making the defense have to account for that. If not, we're going to run the ball for 200 yards or whatever we did the week before [against the Denver Broncos].

"You want to be able to do it all. We showcased that we can throw the ball down the field, we can play action and can also still run the ball."

In 30 touches, Walker was able to outlast many of the Colts' defenders as the game progressed. With quickness, elusiveness and power, Walker forced 15 missed tackles against the Colts, which exceeded his career high of 14 from the previous week against the Broncos, according to Next Gen Stats.

"They packed five guys in there [on the line of scrimmage]," coach Andy Reid said of the Colts' defense. "That's a good front, so we knew it was going to be tough, but we had a good mix going, a few screens and a couple play-action [passes]. We ran the ball efficiently enough. [Walker] got over 100 yards, but he had to earn every bit of it."

Walker became the first Chiefs player since running back Larry Johnson in 2005 to generate 175 or more all-purpose yards in consecutive games.

"You can see what the defense is doing and how they're playing," Walker said of his performance improving after halftime. "I get stronger. The way we condition, it's a lot easier in the game.

"We worked on [our endurance] in training camp with a lot of long practices. We knew what we had to do. When you go through those practices, you have no choice [but to succeed]."

Walker's presence was able to impact the Chiefs' offense even when he didn't touch the ball. Mahomes finished Sunday's game with a career-high 14 completions on play-action passes for 137 yards and two touchdowns.

Mahomes even shared that Walker's play was helpful for tight end Travis Kelce, who led the Chiefs with 101 receiving yards and a touchdown.

"When you run the ball, the play action opens up," Mahomes said. "We built on what we did the week before. Just as much as it's cleaned up the game for me, I think having Kenneth and the way he's runnin

articles.headline: Colts' Shane Steichen defends OT playcalling in loss to Chiefs
articles.description: Colts coach Shane Steichen defended his late-game strategy and playcalling in Sunday night's 33-30 overtime loss to the Chiefs, saying he would have gone for the win on fourth-and-8 had Kansas City showed a favorable defensive coverage.
articles.headlineJa: コルツのシェーン・ステイケン監督、チーフス戦でのOTのプレイコールを擁護
articles.descriptionJa: コルツのシェーン・ステイケン監督は、日曜夜に行われたチーフスとのオーバータイム戦（33-30で敗北）での試合終盤の戦略とプレイコールを擁護し、カンザスシティが有利な守備陣形を見せていれば、4thダウン・アンド・8で勝利を狙いに行っていたと述べた。
articles.body:
KANSAS CITY, Mo. -- Indianapolis Colts coach Shane Steichen defended his late-game strategy and playcalling in Indianapolis' 33-30 overtime loss to the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday night, saying he ultimately was going for the win.

With 4:50 left in overtime, quarterback Daniel Jones connected on a 50-yard strike to receiver Laquon Treadwell, giving the Colts a first-and-10 at the Kansas City 17-yard line.

Trailing 30-27, Steichen then dialed up back-to-back runs for Jonathan Taylor, who collectively lost 3 yards.

Steichen defended the decision and said it was not an attempt to be conservative.

"I was trying to finish the game with [Taylor] with the ball in his hands," Steichen said.

That left the Colts facing a third-and-13 that the Chiefs defended well. Jones dropped back but was flushed from the pocket, running for 5 yards before safety Jaden Hicks pushed him out of bounds. 

Steichen said he was prepared to go for it on the ensuing fourth-and-8 had the Chiefs showed a favorable defensive coverage for the Colts' playcall. A touchdown would have won the game under the NFL's current overtime format.

"We wanted it to be the last possession," Steichen said.

Steichen called timeout, during which he said he told Jones, "If you love it, man, let's go at it. Let's go win this thing. But if it's not the right look ... let's kick the field goal here." 

Kicking a tying field goal presented its own set of challenges, as it meant putting the defense back on the field. The Colts have given up a staggering 1,029 yards in their first two games and struggled against the Chiefs, something that was compounded by starting cornerback Charvarius Ward (groin) having left the game and All-Pro cornerback Sauce Gardner playing through a rib injury.

Ultimately, the Chiefs showed a coverage that was not conducive to the play's success and the Colts took a delay of game penalty and settled for a field goal. Kansas City subsequently drove down the field and won on a 40-yard Harrison Butker field goal as time expired.

Steichen also addressed his decision to defer after the Colts won the overtime coin toss. He said he preferred having the advantage of knowing what his team needed to do after a Kansas City possession.

"If we go first ... [Patrick] Mahomes gets four downs going the other way," Steichen said. "It could go either way in those situations."

articles.headline: Brewers savor franchise-record 98th victory as playoffs loom
articles.description: Milwaukee broke the single-season wins mark it set last season Sunday night, smothering Baltimore 3-0 to improve to 98-58.
articles.headlineJa: ブルワーズがプレーオフを控え球団記録となる98勝目を噛み締める
articles.descriptionJa: ミルウォーキーは日曜夜、ボルチモアを3-0で完封して98勝58敗とし、昨季樹立した単一シーズンの最多勝利記録を更新しました。
articles.body:
BALTIMORE -- The Milwaukee Brewers haven't won more than five games in a row all year. It hasn't stopped them from setting a single-season franchise record for victories.

Milwaukee broke the mark it set last season Sunday night, smothering the Baltimore Orioles 3-0 to improve to 98-58.

"We haven't had these streaks of greatness," manager Pat Murphy said. "We haven't put it all together."

Even without rattling off an extended run, the Brewers have the best record in the majors. They've already clinched their fourth consecutive NL Central title and will make their eighth postseason appearance in nine years. Twice in that span they've advanced to the NL Championship Series, including last year, but they have not reached the World Series since 1982.

Milwaukee completed its ninth series sweep of the season while receiving help from all over the roster. The Brewers stole four bases, got a stellar diving catch from center fielder Garrett Mitchell in the seventh inning and had seven pitchers combine on a four-hit shutout for the record-setting victory with six games left.

"It means a lot," said pitcher Jacob Misiorowski (15-5, 1.86 ERA), who gave up a hit and struck out four in three innings in an abbreviated start designed to manage his workload.

"It's always a big deal to set a new record, a franchise record at that. Hopefully, we get a few more and get to a little bigger number."

Milwaukee enters the final week of the season two games ahead of the Los Angeles Dodgers for the best record in the NL and needs only one more victory or an Atlanta loss to lock up a bye into the division series.

"It's hard to be in this spot to begin with, and I don't think it's appreciated enough," Murphy said. "I think people don't realize how hard it is for any of the 30 teams to put themselves in this position, and that's what makes me proud of these guys. We're not the oldest team, we're not the most experienced, we're not the most talented. We're not the most a lot of things, but for sure they've proven they're a team."
